# S3 Fallback

Version 0.0.2 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A default bucket for instances that have no S3 of their own. You name your S3-compatible backends once, then mount
each kind of file on one: record uploads, backup zips, PITR history, or any extension's own kind. Every instance gets
its own folder in the bucket and can't reach anything outside it. The credentials never reach the instance.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

S3 Fallback is in the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard), so it's built into `pocketone` and every isolate on a
[multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) host has it (Docker containers run stock images). It does nothing until the
`storage` section below mounts a backend. Its main use is a multisite host, where each instance gets its own folder in
one bucket; a single app with mounts keeps its files at the backend's root.

In your own Go build, reconfigure the member instead of adding it again:

```go
set := standard.New()
set.S3Fallback = s3fallback.New(s3fallback.Config{Backends: backends, Mounts: mounts})
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/s3-fallback`.

## Configure

The `storage` section of `pocketone.yaml` is read on first use. Fields set in Go win.

```yaml
storage:
  backends:                        # named S3-compatible destinations
    r2-eu:   { endpoint: https://<account>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, bucket: pocketbase-eu, region: auto, access_key: $R2_KEY, secret: $R2_SECRET }
    b2-cold: { endpoint: ..., bucket: ph-backups, region: ..., access_key: ..., secret: ... }
  mounts:                          # filesystem kind -> backend
    storage:    r2-eu              # record uploads
    backups:    b2-cold            # backup zips
    litestream: r2-eu              # PITR history (ext/pitr)
  # enabled: false                 # off for every instance
```

Each backend also takes `prefix` (prepended to every key, so several deployments can share a bucket) and
`force_path_style` (for MinIO and similar servers). With no mounts the extension does nothing and files stay on local
disk, as in PocketBase.

Each instance can turn it off in its own settings, from `instances.yaml` or a mothership. Only `enabled` is read per
instance; backends and mounts are the operator's:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: blog
    extensions: { storage: { enabled: false } }
```

The old shape (`bucket:` with `uploads:` / `backups:`) still works, with a warning: it becomes a backend named
`default`, mounted for uploads and backups.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `storage:`

A default S3 bucket for apps without their own (on a multisite host, one folder per instance): backends and mounts for uploads, backups, PITR history.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On for every instance unless false; an instance's extensions.storage.enabled overrides it. |
| `backends` | map of object |  | Named S3-compatible destinations: endpoint, bucket, region, access_key, secret, prefix, force_path_style. |
| `mounts` | map of string |  | Filesystem kind (storage, backups, litestream, ...) to backend name. |
| `bucket.endpoint` | string |  | S3 endpoint URL. |
| `bucket.bucket` | string |  | Bucket name. |
| `bucket.region` | string |  | Bucket region (auto for R2). |
| `bucket.access_key` | string |  | Access key id. |
| `bucket.secret` | string |  | Secret key; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `bucket.prefix` | string |  | Prepended to every key, to share a bucket. |
| `bucket.force_path_style` | bool |  | Path-style addressing, for MinIO and similar servers. |
| `uploads` | bool |  | Deprecated: with bucket, false keeps uploads off it. |
| `backups` | bool |  | Deprecated: with bucket, false keeps backups off it. |

## Use

There's nothing to do day to day. To an instance nothing is configured: Settings show S3 off, and uploads, thumbs,
`$app.newFilesystem()` and the Backups screen work as before. Files land in the bucket under
`<prefix>instances/<id>/<kind>/`. Downloads stream through the server, or redirect to the bucket with
[S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect).

When an instance turns on its own S3 (Settings → Files storage, or Settings → Backups), PocketBase's normal code takes
over with the instance's credentials. Files already in the default bucket stay there, as PocketBase's own S3 switch
doesn't move files either.

It applies to instances created with the extension on. Files already on an instance's local disk are not read or moved.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Every instance the set reaches gets the extension. An isolate (Pocker) gets the root `instances/<id>/`. |
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Mount `litestream` and every instance without its own bucket keeps its history there. An instance's own PITR bucket still wins. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | Downloads become signed redirects to the bucket. Nothing to wire: the fenced filesystem signs with its prefix, so S3 Redirect treats it like any S3 mount. |

### Building on S3 Fallback

- **Your own kind.** Any kind an extension asks for through PocketBase's `OnFilesystemCreate` is served when it's mounted.
  PITR's `litestream` works this way. Uploads and backups step aside when the app turned on its own S3; for other
  kinds, the extension asking checks its own app setting first.
- **Go API.** `Bind(app, root)` serves an app's filesystems from the mounts under `root` (`""` for an app that has
  the process to itself, `instances/<id>/` for an isolate, as under Pocker). `FS(root, kind)` returns the same
  fenced filesystem outside a hook; close it when done. `Config()` returns the effective configuration.

## Example

There's no `example/main.go` yet. [`modes_test.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3-fallback/modes_test.go) shows it on the `pocketone` binary, as a single app
and on a multisite host; [`storage_test.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3-fallback/storage_test.go) and [`mounts_test.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3-fallback/mounts_test.go) show it in Go.

## How it works

- PocketBase asks `OnFilesystemCreate` before it creates a filesystem. For a mounted kind, the extension answers with the
  backend, fenced to `<backend prefix><root><kind>/`. An instance can't list, read, write or delete anything outside
  it.
- The fence is a driver that adds the prefix to every key and strips it from listings. Signed download URLs are made
  with the backend's own credentials.

### Status

Works and is tested, in-process and on the `pocketone` binary as a single app and on a multisite host, against an in-memory bucket that checks signed downloads ([`modes_test.go`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/s3-fallback/modes_test.go)); not yet deployed.
